evals.prompt: I will pass in an Azure DevOps work item. Review the user story and list out all the non-functional requirements.
expectations: names concrete non-functional categories such as performance, availability, scalability, usability, or compliance
covers more than one non-functional category, not a single requirement
ties each requirement back to the story or its acceptance criteria rather than giving a generic NFR definition
keeps the non-functional list separate from any security requirements in the output

evals.prompt: I will pass in an Azure DevOps work item. Review the user story and list out all the security requirements.
expectations: names concrete security categories such as authentication, authorisation, encryption, input validation, or audit
covers more than one security category, not a single requirement
ties each security requirement back to the part of the story that creates it rather than giving a generic security definition
keeps the security list separate from the non-functional requirements in the output
